proofs.proof_tex:
Fix \(n\ge 12\), \(0<h\le r_0\), a finite integer \(k\ge1\), and positive integers \(J_\pi,J_\mu\).  Then \(m=\lfloor n/3\rfloor\ge4\), so the ordered quadratic average in Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}private\text{-}higher\text{-}order\text{-}learner}\) is well defined.  By Assumptions \(\mathrm{ass{:}consistency}\) and \(\mathrm{ass{:}bounded\text{-}outcomes}\), every observed record under any \(Q\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{att}}\) lies almost surely in the privacy domain
\[
 \mathcal O_0=[0,1]^d\times\{0,1\}\times[0,1].
\]
The privacy calculation below is deterministic on \(\mathcal O_0^n\) and therefore does not otherwise depend on \(Q\).

First condition on arbitrary realized projected pilots \((\bar\pi,\bar\mu)\).  If a projection set in Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}private\text{-}higher\text{-}order\text{-}learner}\) is nonempty, membership of the projection in that set gives the relevant range restriction; if it is empty, the prescribed fallback gives the same restriction.  Hence, using \(0<\kappa<1/2\),
\[
 \kappa\le \bar\pi(x)\le1-\kappa,
 \qquad 0\le\bar\mu(x)\le1
 \quad (x\in\mathcal X).
\tag{1}
\]
For \(o=(x,a,y)\in\mathcal O_0\), all scalar factors in the kernels involving \(a\), \(a-\bar\pi(x)\), or \(y-\bar\mu(x)\) consequently have absolute value at most one.  The basis bounds and \(K_h\le h^{-d}\) from the same definition therefore imply
\[
 \|\operatorname{vec}L_Q(o)\|_2\le c_\rho^2h^{-d},
 \qquad
 \|L_R(o)\|_2\le c_\rho h^{-d}.
\]
Thus, with \(c_L=(c_\rho^4+c_\rho^2)^{1/2}\),
\[
 \|L(o)\|_2\le c_Lh^{-d}.
\tag{2}
\]
Moreover, Cauchy--Schwarz and the support and normalization of \(b_{h,k}\) give
\[
 |b_{h,k}(x)^{\mathsf T}b_{h,k}(x')|
 \le c_b^2kh^{-d}
\]
when both arguments are in \(C_h\), while the left side is zero if either argument is outside \(C_h\).  It follows that
\[
 \|\operatorname{vec}H_Q(o,o')\|_2
 \le c_b^2c_\rho^2kh^{-2d},
 \qquad
 \|H_R(o,o')\|_2
 \le c_b^2c_\rho kh^{-2d}.
\]
With \(c_H=c_b^2(c_\rho^4+c_\rho^2)^{1/2}\), the deterministic clipping radii consequently satisfy
\[
 \Lambda_L\le c_Lh^{-d},
 \qquad
 \Lambda_H\le c_Hkh^{-2d}.
\tag{3}
\]
Equations (1)--(3) hold uniformly over all pilot realizations and all \(Q\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{att}}\).

Let two main-block samples differ by replacement at index \(r\).  The clipped linear average changes by at most \(2\Lambda_L/m\).  Exactly \(2(m-1)\) ordered pairs, namely \((r,j)\) and \((j,r)\) for \(j\ne r\), can change in the quadratic average.  Each changed clipped vector differs from its old value by at most \(2\Lambda_H\).  The triangle inequality therefore yields
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \|T_*(D_*)-T_*(D_*')\|_2
 &\le {2\Lambda_L\over m}
   +{2(m-1)\,2\Lambda_H\over m(m-1)}\\
 &= {2\Lambda_L+4\Lambda_H\over m}\\
 &\le {C_\Delta\over m}\{h^{-d}+kh^{-2d}\},
 \end{aligned}
\tag{4}
\]
where \(C_\Delta=\max\{2c_L,4c_H\}\).  This proves the asserted conditional sensitivity bound, with the stated dependence of its constant.

For each \(u\in\{\pi,\mu\}\), replacement of one record in its pilot block changes the unnoised sufficient-statistic average by
\[
 \left\|m^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^m z_u(O_i)
       -m^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^m z_u(O_i')\right\|_2
 =m^{-1}\|z_u(o)-z_u(o')\|_2\le\Delta_u.
\tag{5}
\]
The supremum defining \(\Delta_u\) is finite because each fixed finite-dimensional spline coordinate is bounded on the compact cube and \((a,y)\in\{0,1\}\times[0,1]\).  Equation (4) similarly shows that \(\overline\Delta_*=(2\Lambda_L+4\Lambda_H)/m\) is a valid replacement sensitivity conditional on the pilots.

The symbol domains give \(0<\epsilon_n\le1\) and \(0<\delta_n<1/2\).  Hence
\[
 0<\epsilon_n^\circ=\min\{\epsilon_n,1/2\}<1,
 \qquad
 c_{\delta_n}>\sqrt{2\log(1.25/\delta_n)}.
\]
Applying Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}gaussian\text{-}mechanism\text{-}replacement}\) to (5) proves that each pilot release is \((\epsilon_n^\circ,\delta_n)\)-differentially private on its own block.  Conditional on every fixed pilot realization, the same lemma applied to (4) proves that the main release is \((\epsilon_n^\circ,\delta_n)\)-differentially private on \(D_*\).

We verify the adaptive parallel accountant directly.  Let \(Z_\pi^{\mathrm{rel}},Z_\mu^{\mathrm{rel}}\) be the pilot releases, let \(W^{\mathrm{rel}}\) be the main release, and put \(\mathcal T=(Z_\pi^{\mathrm{rel}},Z_\mu^{\mathrm{rel}},W^{\mathrm{rel}})\).  If adjacent full samples differ in \(D_*\), the joint pilot law \(\nu\) is common.  For a transcript event \(E\), let \(E_z\) be its section at pilot value \(z\), and let \(K_D(z,\cdot)\) be the conditional main-release law.  Conditional privacy and integration against \(\nu\) give
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \Pr_D(\mathcal T\in E)
 &=\int K_D(z,E_z)\,d\nu(z)\\
 &\le e^{\epsilon_n^\circ}\int K_{D'}(z,E_z)\,d\nu(z)+\delta_n\\
 &=e^{\epsilon_n^\circ}\Pr_{D'}(\mathcal T\in E)+\delta_n.
 \end{aligned}
\tag{6}
\]
If the replacement lies in \(D_\pi\), condition on the unchanged blocks.  Once \(Z_\pi^{\mathrm{rel}}=z\) is fixed, all later randomized operations define the same Markov kernel \(K(z,\cdot)\) under the two adjacent inputs.  For \(g(z)=K(z,E)\in[0,1]\), the layer-cake identity and pilot privacy imply
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \int g\,d\mathsf P_D
 &=\int_0^1\mathsf P_D\{g>t\}\,dt\\
 &\le\int_0^1\{e^{\epsilon_n^\circ}\mathsf P_{D'}\{g>t\}+\delta_n\}\,dt\\
 &=e^{\epsilon_n^\circ}\int g\,d\mathsf P_{D'}+\delta_n.
 \end{aligned}
\tag{7}
\]
This is the privacy inequality for the full transcript.  The argument for a replacement in \(D_\mu\) is identical, and a replacement among the at most two discarded observations leaves the transcript unchanged.  Equations (6)--(7) cover all cases, proving that \(\mathcal T\) is replacement \((\epsilon_n^\circ,\delta_n)\)-differentially private.  Since \(\epsilon_n^\circ\le\epsilon_n\), it is also replacement \((\epsilon_n,\delta_n)\)-differentially private.

All pilot reconstruction, metric projection, spectral flooring, inversion, and evaluation operations in Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}private\text{-}higher\text{-}order\text{-}learner}\) are measurable post-processing of \(\mathcal T\).  In the corrected Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}private\text{-}confidence\text{-}interval}\), the map
\[
 \widehat\tau_{\mathrm{DP}}(x_0;h,k)
 \longmapsto
 \bar\tau_{\mathrm{DP}}(x_0;h,k)
 =\max\{-1,\min\{1,\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{DP}}(x_0;h,k)\}\}
\]
is deterministic post-processing, as are formation of the interval with deterministic radius \(R_n(h,k)\) and intersection with \([-1,1]\).  Applying the transcript privacy inequality to inverse images of output events proves that both \(\mathsf M_{h,k,J_\pi,J_\mu}^{\mathrm{DP}}\) and the corrected \(C_n(h,k)\) are replacement \((\epsilon_n,\delta_n)\)-differentially private.  Thus clipping the released center changes neither the accountant nor the sensitivity bound (4).

Fix \(0<h\le r_0\), a finite integer \(k\ge1\) satisfying \(mh^d\ge C_S^2\log(8/\eta)\), and integers \(J_\pi,J_\mu\ge1\).  Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}private\text{-}release\text{-}and\text{-}sensitivity}\), applied to the corrected Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}private\text{-}confidence\text{-}interval}\), proves that \(C_n(h,k)\) is replacement \((\epsilon_n,\delta_n)\)-differentially private.

For \(Q\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{att}}\), set
\[
 R=R_n(h,k)=B(h,k)+S(h,k,\eta)+G(h,k,\eta,\epsilon_n,\delta_n)
\]
and define the event
\[
 E_Q=\left\{
 |\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{DP}}(x_0;h,k)-\tau_Q(x_0)|\le R
 \right\}.
\tag{1}
\]
Every summand defining \(R\) is nonnegative.  The effective-sample condition permits application of the already proved Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}uniform\text{-}remainder\text{-}unrestricted\text{-}rank}\), which gives
\[
 \Pr_Q(E_Q)\ge1-\eta.
\tag{2}
\]
Proposition \(\mathrm{prop{:}attainable\text{-}inclusion}\) gives \(Q\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{full}}\), and Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}pointwise\text{-}identification}\) therefore gives
\[
 \theta_Q:=\tau_Q^{\mathrm c}(x_0)=\tau_Q(x_0).
\tag{3}
\]
Assumption \(\mathrm{ass{:}bounded\text{-}outcomes}\) implies \(-1\le Y(1)-Y(0)\le1\) almost surely.  Conditional expectation preserves these bounds, so
\[
 \theta_Q\in[-1,1].
\tag{4}
\]

Let \(\Pi(t)=\max\{-1,\min\{1,t\}\}\), so the corrected definition has \(\bar\tau_{\mathrm{DP}}(x_0;h,k)=\Pi(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{DP}}(x_0;h,k))\).  For any \(\theta\in[-1,1]\), a three-case calculation gives
\[
 |\Pi(t)-\theta|\le|t-\theta|:
\tag{5}
\]
if \(t\in[-1,1]\) equality holds; if \(t>1\), then \(0\le1-\theta\le t-\theta\); and if \(t<-1\), then \(0\le\theta+1\le\theta-t\).  Combining (1), (3), (4), and (5), on \(E_Q\) one has
\[
 |\bar\tau_{\mathrm{DP}}(x_0;h,k)-\theta_Q|
 \le|\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{DP}}(x_0;h,k)-\theta_Q|
 \le R.
\tag{6}
\]
Thus \(\theta_Q\) belongs both to
\([\bar\tau_{\mathrm{DP}}-R,\bar\tau_{\mathrm{DP}}+R]\) and, by (4), to \([-1,1]\).  The corrected definition and (6) imply
\[
 E_Q\subseteq\{\theta_Q\in C_n(h,k)\}.
\tag{7}
\]
Moreover, on every transcript, including outside \(E_Q\), one has \(\bar\tau_{\mathrm{DP}}\in[-1,1]\) and \(R\ge0\).  Therefore \(\bar\tau_{\mathrm{DP}}\) itself lies in both intervals whose intersection defines \(C_n(h,k)\).  Hence \(C_n(h,k)\) is always a nonempty closed interval.

Taking probabilities in (7), using (2), and then taking the infimum over \(Q\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{att}}\) proves
\[
 \inf_{Q\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{att}}}
 \Pr_Q\{\tau_Q^{\mathrm c}(x_0)\in C_n(h,k)\}\ge1-\eta.
\]
The probability in (2) already integrates all sample blocks and Gaussian releases by Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}uniform\text{-}remainder\text{-}unrestricted\text{-}rank}\).  No restriction relating \(k\) to \(mh^d\) was introduced.

Put
\[
 x=\log(8/\eta),\qquad M=mh^d,\qquad \ell=hk^{-1/d},
\]
and define
\[
 r_o=n^{-1/(2+d/\gamma)},
 \qquad
 r_2=n^{-1/\{1+d/(2\gamma)+d/(2q)\}}.
\tag{1}
\]
The symbol domains give \(d\ge1\), \(q=\alpha+\beta>0\), \(\gamma>0\), and \(0<\eta<1/4\), so these quantities are positive and finite.  Since \(n\ge12\) and \(m=\lfloor n/3\rfloor\),
\[
 n/4\le m\le n/3.
\tag{2}
\]

Because \(s=q/2\), the low-smoothness condition in Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}phase\text{-}rate}\) is
\[
 q<{d\over2\{1+d/(2\gamma)\}}.
\tag{3}
\]
Furthermore,
\[
 1+{d\over2\gamma}+{d\over2q}>2+{d\over\gamma}
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 q<{d\over2\{1+d/(2\gamma)\}}.
\tag{4}
\]
At equality the two powers agree.  Thus the two branches of that definition give
\[
 r_{\mathrm{np}}=r_o\vee r_2.
\tag{5}
\]
Set
\[
 R=r_{\mathrm{np}}\vee r_{\mathrm{reg}}\vee r_{\mathrm{ho}}
   =r_{\mathrm{up}},
 \qquad
 t=1\wedge R=1\wedge r_{\mathrm{up}}.
\tag{6}
\]
Fix a constant \(0<t_0<1\wedge r_0^\gamma\).  When \(t<t_0\), equations (5)--(6) imply \(t=R\) and
\[
 t\ge r_o,\qquad t\ge r_2,
 \qquad t\ge r_{\mathrm{reg}},\qquad t\ge r_{\mathrm{ho}}.
\tag{7}
\]

For every admissible \((h,k)\), one has \(0<\ell\le h\le r_0\le1/4\).  Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}bias\text{-}envelope}\) and \(\alpha>0\) hence give
\[
 B(h,k)=C_B\{h^\gamma+\ell^q+h^\gamma\ell^\alpha\}
 \le C\{h^\gamma+\ell^q\}.
\tag{8}
\]
Here and below \(C\) denotes a finite constant depending only on the fixed class constants and \(\eta\).  If
\[
 a=M^{-1/2},\qquad b={\sqrt{k}\over M},
\tag{9}
\]
then Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}sampling\text{-}envelope}\) is exactly
\[
 S(h,k,\eta)=C_S\left\{
 \sqrt{x(a^2+b^2)}+xa^2+x^{3/2}ab+x^2b^2
 \right\}.
\tag{10}
\]
No rank inequality is used in (10).  Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}privacy\text{-}envelope}\), the definition of \(N_{\mathrm{priv}}\), equation (2), and the fixed value of \(\eta\) give
\[
 G(h,k,\eta,\epsilon_n,\delta_n)
 \le C N_{\mathrm{priv}}^{-1}\{h^{-d}+kh^{-2d}\}
 =C N_{\mathrm{priv}}^{-1}\{h^{-d}+h^{-d}\ell^{-d}\}.
\tag{11}
\]

Suppose first that \(q<\gamma\) and \(t<t_0\).  Choose
\[
 h=t^{1/\gamma},\qquad \ell_0=t^{1/q},
 \qquad K=(h/\ell_0)^d,\qquad k=\lceil K\rceil.
\tag{12}
\]
Since \(0<t<1\) and \(q<\gamma\), \(K\ge1\), whence
\[
 K\le k\le2K,
 \qquad 2^{-1/d}\ell_0\le\ell=hk^{-1/d}\le\ell_0.
\tag{13}
\]
Equations (8), (12), and (13) yield
\[
 B(h,k)\le C\{t+t+t\ell^\alpha\}\le Ct.
\tag{14}
\]
By (2), (7), and the definitions in (1),
\[
 a=m^{-1/2}t^{-d/(2\gamma)}
 \le2n^{-1/2}t^{-d/(2\gamma)}\le2t,
\tag{15}
\]
and
\[
 b\le{\sqrt2\over mh^{d/2}\ell_0^{d/2}}
 \le4\sqrt2\,n^{-1}t^{-d/(2\gamma)-d/(2q)}
 \le4\sqrt2\,t.
\tag{16}
\]
Using \(\sqrt{a^2+b^2}\le a+b\), \(t\le1\), and (15)--(16) in (10) gives
\[
 S(h,k,\eta)\le Ct.
\tag{17}
\]
On this branch \(\bar q=q\), so Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}phase\text{-}rate}\) reads
\[
 r_{\mathrm{reg}}=N_{\mathrm{priv}}^{-1/(1+d/\gamma)},
 \qquad
 r_{\mathrm{ho}}=N_{\mathrm{priv}}^{-1/(1+d/\gamma+d/q)}.
\tag{18}
\]
The final two inequalities in (7) are therefore equivalent to
\[
 N_{\mathrm{priv}}^{-1}t^{-d/\gamma}\le t,
 \qquad
 N_{\mathrm{priv}}^{-1}t^{-d/\gamma-d/q}\le t.
\tag{19}
\]
Equations (11)--(13) and (19) imply
\[
 G(h,k,\eta,\epsilon_n,\delta_n)\le Ct.
\tag{20}
\]
Combining (14), (17), and (20) gives
\[
 B(h,k)+S(h,k,\eta)+G(h,k,\eta,\epsilon_n,\delta_n)\le Ct.
\tag{21}
\]
This construction remains admissible when \(k>M\), because none of the three envelope definitions imposes a rank cap.

Now suppose \(q\ge\gamma\) and \(t<t_0\).  Choose
\[
 h=t^{1/\gamma},\qquad k=1,\qquad\ell=h.
\tag{22}
\]
Since \(h<1\), \(q\ge\gamma\), and \(\alpha>0\), equation (8) gives \(B(h,1)\le Ct\).  Equation (15) remains valid, while \(b=M^{-1}=a^2\le4t^2\); hence (10) gives \(S(h,1,\eta)\le Ct\).  Here \(\bar q=\gamma\), and therefore
\[
 r_{\mathrm{ho}}=N_{\mathrm{priv}}^{-1/(1+2d/\gamma)}.
\tag{23}
\]
The inequality \(t\ge r_{\mathrm{ho}}\) is equivalent to
\[
 N_{\mathrm{priv}}^{-1}t^{-2d/\gamma}\le t.
\tag{24}
\]
Since \(h<1\), equations (11), (22), and (24) give \(G(h,1,\eta,\epsilon_n,\delta_n)\le Ct\), and (21) follows on this branch as well.  Equations (18)--(20) give the \(q\)-branch for \(q<\gamma\), while (23)--(24) give \(N_{\mathrm{priv}}^{-\gamma/(\gamma+2d)}\) for \(q\ge\gamma\).

We next verify feasibility and existence of the deterministic minimizer.  In both branches, \(h=t^{1/\gamma}<r_0\).  Equations (2), (7), and the definition of \(r_o\) imply
\[
 mh^d=mt^{d/\gamma}
 \ge{1\over4}n^{2\gamma/(2\gamma+d)}\longrightarrow\infty.
\tag{25}
\]
Thus the comparison pair satisfies \(mh^d\ge C_S^2x\) for all sufficiently large \(n\).  For those \(n\), the feasible bandwidth set is the nonempty compact interval
\[
 I_n=[\{C_S^2x/m\}^{1/d},r_0].
\tag{26}
\]
Let \(F_n(h,k)=B(h,k)+S(h,k,\eta)+G(h,k,\eta,\epsilon_n,\delta_n)\).  Since \((r_0,1)\) is feasible, \(V_n=F_n(r_0,1)<\infty\).  The last nonnegative term of the sampling envelope and \(h\le r_0\) imply
\[
 F_n(h,k)\ge {C_Sx^2\over m^2r_0^{2d}}k=:c_nk,
 \qquad c_n>0.
\tag{27}
\]
Therefore no \(k>V_n/c_n\) minimizes \(F_n\).  For each of the finitely many remaining positive integers \(k\), the map \(h\mapsto F_n(h,k)\) is continuous on \(I_n\), so it attains a minimum.  Minimizing over that finite collection and resolving ties lexicographically produces the asserted deterministic minimizer \((\widehat h,\widehat k)\).

When \(t<t_0\), feasibility of the corresponding comparison pair and (21) yield
\[
 F_n(\widehat h,\widehat k)\le Ct.
\tag{28}
\]
Under the corrected Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}private\text{-}confidence\text{-}interval}\), its center \(\bar\tau_{\mathrm{DP}}\) always belongs to \([-1,1]\) and every envelope is nonnegative.  Hence the intersection defining \(C_n(\widehat h,\widehat k)\) is nonempty, and deterministically
\[
 \operatorname{length}\{C_n(\widehat h,\widehat k)\}
 \le 2F_n(\widehat h,\widehat k)\wedge2.
\tag{29}
\]
Equations (28)--(29) bound the length by \(2Ct\) if \(t<t_0\).  If \(t\ge t_0\), (29) gives
\[
 \operatorname{length}\{C_n(\widehat h,\widehat k)\}
 \le2\le(2/t_0)t.
\tag{30}
\]
These bounds are pointwise in the transcript and uniform over \(Q\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{att}}\) and the deterministic pilot dimensions.  Taking expectation and the supremum over \(Q\), then using (6), proves
\[
 \sup_{Q\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{att}}}
 \mathbb E_Q[\operatorname{length}\{C_n(\widehat h,\widehat k)\}]
 \le C_L\{1\wedge r_{\mathrm{up}}\}.
\]
The threshold \(n_0\) used in (25)--(27) depends only on the fixed class constants and \(\eta\).  Clipping the center changes neither the deterministic envelope optimization nor any rate calculation, and this proof makes no full-class lower or frontier claim.

We first transfer the ordinary two-law lower construction from Theorem \(\mathrm{thm{:}full\text{-}class\text{-}ordinary\text{-}lower}\) to the attainable class.  Use the bump \(\varphi\), the constants \(p_*=\min\{1/4,L_\mu/2\}>0\) and \(a_*>0\), and
\[
 g_h(x)=a_*h^\gamma\varphi((x-x_0)/h)
\tag{1}
\]
from that theorem's proof.  Its H\"older and range calculations give, for \(0<h\le r_0\),
\[
 g_h\in\mathcal H^\gamma(L_\tau;\mathcal X),
 \qquad 0\le g_h\le p_*/2,
 \qquad g_h(x_0)=a_*h^\gamma.
\tag{2}
\]
Let \(Q_0,Q_h\) be its two full-data laws: under both, \(X\) is uniform on \(\mathcal X\), \(A\mid X\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(\kappa)\), and \(A\) is conditionally independent of \((Y(0),Y(1))\) given \(X\).  Under \(Q_0\), the conditionally independent potential outcomes are Bernoulli with mean \(p_*\).  Under \(Q_h\), their conditional means are
\[
 \mathbb E_{Q_h}[Y(0)\mid X=x]=p_*,
 \qquad
 \mathbb E_{Q_h}[Y(1)\mid X=x]=p_*+g_h(x).
\tag{3}
\]
In both laws, define \(Y=AY(1)+(1-A)Y(0)\).

These laws satisfy every member property in Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}attainable\text{-}law\text{-}class}\).  The last display gives Assumption \(\mathrm{ass{:}consistency}\), and the specified conditional independence gives Assumption \(\mathrm{ass{:}ignorability}\).  The potential outcomes lie in \(\{0,1\}\), so Assumption \(\mathrm{ass{:}bounded\text{-}outcomes}\) holds; moreover (2) gives
\[
 0<p_*\le p_*+g_h(x)\le3p_*/2\le3/8<1,
\]
so all Bernoulli laws are well defined.  Since \(0<\kappa<1/2\), the constant propensity obeys Assumption \(\mathrm{ass{:}overlap}\), and its H\"older norm is \(\kappa\le L_\pi\), by the proposition's premise.  The control regression is the constant \(p_*\), whose H\"older norm is at most \(L_\mu/2\), while the CATE is zero under \(Q_0\) and equals \(g_h\) under \(Q_h\); hence Assumptions \(\mathrm{ass{:}control\text{-}holder}\) and \(\mathrm{ass{:}cate\text{-}holder}\) follow from the definition of \(p_*\) and (2).  Finally, the design density is one almost everywhere, which is Assumption \(\mathrm{ass{:}uniform\text{-}design}\).  Therefore
\[
 Q_0,Q_h\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{att}}.
\tag{4}
\]

Let \(P_0,P_h\) be their one-record observed laws.  The divergence, one-record total-variation, and separation calculations in Theorem \(\mathrm{thm{:}full\text{-}class\text{-}ordinary\text{-}lower}\) give constants \(C_\chi,C_v\in(0,\infty)\) for which
\[
 \chi^2(P_h\Vert P_0)=C_\chi h^{2\gamma+d},
 \quad
 \|P_h-P_0\|_{\mathrm{TV}}=C_vh^{\gamma+d},
 \quad
 |\tau_{Q_h}^{\mathrm c}(x_0)-\tau_{Q_0}^{\mathrm c}(x_0)|=a_*h^\gamma.
\tag{5}
\]
Its product-divergence argument and Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}dp\text{-}hamming\text{-}transport}\), using \(\delta_n\le c_0/n\), provide constants \(c_1,c_2\in(0,r_0]\) such that
\[
 h_1=c_1n^{-1/(2\gamma+d)},
 \qquad
 h_2=c_2\{1\wedge(n\epsilon_n)^{-1}\}^{1/(\gamma+d)}
\tag{6}
\]
obey, for every replacement \((\epsilon_n,\delta_n)\)-private kernel \(\mathsf K\),
\[
 \|P_{h_j}^n\mathsf K-P_0^n\mathsf K\|_{\mathrm{TV}}\le1/8,
 \qquad j\in\{1,2\}.
\tag{7}
\]

Take any \(C\in\mathfrak C_n^{\mathrm{att}}\) with release kernel \(\mathsf K\), and fix either \(h=h_1\) or \(h=h_2\).  Write \(\theta_0=\tau_{Q_0}^{\mathrm c}(x_0)\), \(\theta_h=\tau_{Q_h}^{\mathrm c}(x_0)\), \(\nu_0=P_0^n\mathsf K\), and \(\nu_h=P_h^n\mathsf K\).  By (4) and attainable-class honesty,
\[
 \nu_0\{\theta_0\in C\}\ge1-\eta,
 \qquad
 \nu_h\{\theta_h\in C\}\ge1-\eta.
\]
Equation (7), followed by the union bound, gives
\[
 \nu_0\{\theta_0\in C,\theta_h\in C\}
 \ge (1-\eta)+(1-\eta-1/8)-1
 =1-2\eta-1/8>3/8.
\tag{8}
\]
On the event in (8), the interval \(C\) contains both target values, so (5) implies that its length is at least \(a_*h^\gamma\).  Hence
\[
 \mathbb E_{Q_0}[\operatorname{length}(C)]\ge(3a_*/8)h^\gamma.
\tag{9}
\]
Applying (9) to both bandwidths in (6), taking their maximum, then taking the supremum over \(Q\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{att}}\) and infimum over \(C\in\mathfrak C_n^{\mathrm{att}}\), proves the stated lower inequality.

For the upper inequality, put
\[
 a_n=1\wedge r_{\mathrm{up}},
 \qquad
 b_n=1\wedge\left[n^{-\beta/(2\beta+d)}
          \vee N_{\mathrm{priv}}^{-\beta/(\beta+d)}\right].
\tag{10}
\]
Choose the deterministic minimizing \((h,k)\) from Theorem \(\mathrm{thm{:}phase\text{-}sensitive\text{-}expected\text{-}length}\) and fixed deterministic pilot dimensions.  Under the corrected Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}private\text{-}confidence\text{-}interval}\), the released center \(\bar\tau_{\mathrm{DP}}\) lies in \([-1,1]\) and the radius is nonnegative, so the resulting intersection contains \(\bar\tau_{\mathrm{DP}}\) on every transcript.  It is therefore literally a nonempty random interval.  Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}private\text{-}release\text{-}and\text{-}sensitivity}\) and Theorem \(\mathrm{thm{:}honest\text{-}private\text{-}pointwise\text{-}interval\text{-}unrestricted\text{-}rank}\) make this higher-order candidate \(C_n^{\mathrm{HO}}\) an element of \(\mathfrak C_n^{\mathrm{att}}\), while the phase-sensitive theorem gives
\[
 \sup_{Q\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{att}}}
 \mathbb E_Q[\operatorname{length}(C_n^{\mathrm{HO}})]
 \le C_{\mathrm{HO}}a_n.
\tag{11}
\]
The direct interval \(C_n^{\mathrm{dir}}(h_n)\) in Theorem \(\mathrm{thm{:}full\text{-}class\text{-}direct\text{-}regression\text{-}upper}\) is replacement private, nonempty, and honest on \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{full}}\).  Proposition \(\mathrm{prop{:}attainable\text{-}inclusion}\) therefore implies that it belongs to \(\mathfrak C_n^{\mathrm{att}}\), with
\[
 \sup_{Q\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{att}}}
 \mathbb E_Q[\operatorname{length}\{C_n^{\mathrm{dir}}(h_n)\}]
 \le C_{\mathrm{dir}}b_n.
\tag{12}
\]
Equivalently, a public deterministic selector may release only \(C_n^{\mathrm{HO}}\) when \(a_n\le b_n\), and only \(C_n^{\mathrm{dir}}(h_n)\) otherwise.  Because it depends only on public parameters and runs exactly one mechanism, it incurs no privacy composition.  Equations (11)--(12) give
\[
 \mathcal L_n^*(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{att}})
 \le\min\{C_{\mathrm{HO}}a_n,C_{\mathrm{dir}}b_n\}
 \le\max\{C_{\mathrm{HO}},C_{\mathrm{dir}}\}\min\{a_n,b_n\},
\]
which is the stated upper inequality.

Finally suppose \(q\ge\gamma\), \(\beta<\gamma<2\beta\), and \(N_{\mathrm{priv}}=n^{c_{\mathrm p}}\), with \(c_{\mathrm p}\) satisfying (2) in the proposition.  Since \(s=q/2\ge\gamma/2\) and
\[
 {\gamma\over2}>{d/4\over1+d/(2\gamma)},
\]
Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}phase\text{-}rate}\) gives
\[
 r_{\mathrm{np}}=n^{-\gamma/(2\gamma+d)},
 \quad
 r_{\mathrm{reg}}=n^{-c_{\mathrm p}\gamma/(\gamma+d)},
 \quad
 r_{\mathrm{ho}}=n^{-c_{\mathrm p}\gamma/(\gamma+2d)}.
\tag{13}
\]
The first restriction on \(c_{\mathrm p}\) makes the last term dominate the first for sufficiently large \(n\), and it always dominates the middle term.  Thus
\[
 a_n=n^{-c_{\mathrm p}\gamma/(\gamma+2d)}.
\tag{14}
\]
The second restriction on \(c_{\mathrm p}\) makes the privacy term dominate the sampling term in \(b_n\), so
\[
 b_n=n^{-c_{\mathrm p}\beta/(\beta+d)}.
\tag{15}
\]
Because \(\gamma<2\beta\) is equivalent to
\[
 {\beta\over\beta+d}>{\gamma\over\gamma+2d},
\]
equations (14)--(15) imply
\[
 {b_n\over a_n}
 =n^{-c_{\mathrm p}\{\beta/(\beta+d)-\gamma/(\gamma+2d)\}}
 \longrightarrow0.
\]
This proves the asserted strict polynomial improvement.  Every lower and upper comparison above is on \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{att}}\); no step resolves the separate full-class frontier.

proposed_definition_changes.reason: Clipping the released center before interval formation guarantees that the intersection is a nonempty interval on every transcript.  Projection onto \([-1,1]\) cannot increase error from the causal target, which itself lies in \([-1,1]\), so privacy, coverage, the deterministic length bound, and all rates are unchanged.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The advertised observed-law interval functional must use the corrected clipped center from Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}private\text{-}confidence\text{-}interval}\).

prose_updates.tldr: The paper constructs replacement-private, finite-sample honest pointwise CATE intervals on the uniform-design attainable class \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{att}}\).  The higher-order interval clips its released center to \([-1,1]\) before adding the deterministic radius, so it is a nonempty random interval on every transcript; projection cannot increase error from the bounded CATE target.  It achieves \(1\wedge r_{\mathrm{up}}\), while the fixed-dimensional direct-regression interval proved on \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{full}}\) remains valid after restriction to \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{att}}\).  A public selector therefore gives the attainable-class upper \(C\min\{1\wedge r_{\mathrm{up}},1\wedge[n^{-\beta/(2\beta+d)}\vee N_{\mathrm{priv}}^{-\beta/(\beta+d)}]\}\); the same uniform-design witness used for the ordinary full-class lower belongs to the attainable class, yielding the corresponding two-sided nonsharp bracket.  On the unchanged full class, only the separate ordinary \(\gamma\)-smooth lower and \(\beta\)-smooth direct-regression upper are certified, and the exact private confidence frontier remains open.

project_justification.fill: The project privatizes every pilot and localized moment for the attainable higher-order construction, clips the released center before interval formation, and proves unrestricted-finite-rank concentration, transcript-wise nonemptiness, uniform finite-sample coverage, and the phase-sensitive mean interval length upper \(1\wedge r_{\mathrm{up}}\) on \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{att}}\).  It also proves a fixed-dimensional direct-regression interval on \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{full}}\), which restricts to the attainable class.  Combining the two by a public deterministic selector and observing that the ordinary lower-bound witness itself has uniform design gives the best certified attainable-class bracket: under \(L_\pi\ge\kappa\), \(\delta_n\le c_0/n\), and sufficiently large \(n\), its lower endpoint is \(c[n^{-\gamma/(2\gamma+d)}\vee\{1\wedge(n\epsilon_n)^{-\gamma/(\gamma+d)}\}]\) and its upper endpoint is \(C\min\{1\wedge r_{\mathrm{up}},1\wedge[n^{-\beta/(2\beta+d)}\vee N_{\mathrm{priv}}^{-\beta/(\beta+d)}]\}\).  Separately, the unchanged full class retains its nonsharp ordinary lower versus direct-regression upper bracket; the attainable higher-order upper is not transferred back to that class, and exact full-class sharpness remains unresolved.

prose_updates.honest_scope: Settled results are replacement privacy and uniform finite-sample coverage of the explicit clipped-center higher-order interval on \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{att}}\), including its nonemptiness on every transcript, its achieved length upper \(1\wedge r_{\mathrm{up}}\), the corrected construction-specific privacy-free reduction with no rank floor, and the attainable-class nonsharp minimax bracket obtained by taking the better of that interval and the restricted direct-regression interval.  The bracket's lower witness has uniform design and satisfies every attainable assumption.  The attainable class remains a restricted submodel; its higher-order upper is not transferred to \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{full}}\).  On the full class, the settled results are the ordinary lower limitation and the fixed-dimensional direct-regression coverage and upper bound, giving \(c[n^{-\gamma/(2\gamma+d)}\vee\{1\wedge(n\epsilon_n)^{-\gamma/(\gamma+d)}\}]\le\mathcal L_n^*(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{full}})\le C[1\wedge\{n^{-\beta/(2\beta+d)}\vee N_{\mathrm{priv}}^{-\beta/(\beta+d)}\}]\) under \(L_\pi\ge\kappa\), \(\delta_n\le c_0/n\), and sufficiently large \(n\).  Whether either bracket is tight, including whether a \(q\)-driven or private-Gram branch is unavoidable, remains unresolved; in particular, the full-class OEQ stays open.

statement_notes.justification: Every pilot and every higher-order moment is protected under one explicit replacement-privacy accountant, and clipping the released center is certified post-processing.
statement_notes.consumer: Privacy officers can audit the release ledger, including center clipping and interval formation, without treating nuisance fits or the quadratic correction as unprotected preprocessing.

statement_notes.justification: The headline converts a fully privatized higher-order CATE learner into an honest, transcript-wise nonempty pointwise causal interval without an artificial cap on the finite higher-order basis dimension.
statement_notes.consumer: A hospital can release a nonempty confidence interval for the treatment effect at a prespecified anchor point while protecting every record.

statement_notes.justification: On \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{att}}\), the result gives an auditable privacy phase diagram for the saturated achieved length \(1\wedge(r_{\mathrm{np}}\vee r_{\mathrm{reg}}\vee r_{\mathrm{ho}})\); clipping the center preserves the deterministic bound \(2R_n\wedge2\) and every tuning calculation.
statement_notes.consumer: Study designers working in the attainable uniform-design model can select bandwidth, higher-order dimension, and privacy budget to meet a prespecified interval-width requirement with a release that is always an interval.

statement_notes.justification: The proposition records the strongest certified two-sided mean-length result on \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{att}}\) by combining the transcript-wise nonempty higher-order interval with the restricted full-class direct interval.
statement_notes.consumer: A study designer can use a public rate comparison to select the narrower of two private honest nonempty pointwise CATE intervals without paying privacy composition.
